title: Cart screen and checkout UI
idea: The cart frontend is a cart screen driven by one reducer: quantity edits show at once and roll back on failure, and checkout can never place two orders.
points: `CartPage` renders state and dispatches events; the reducer owns every screen rule.
Edits are optimistic; a failed save restores the last server-confirmed quantity.
One Idempotency-Key per checkout survives retries, so a lost response never duplicates orders.
Follow-ups: merge guest carts at login, queue flash-sale checkouts, add coupons as PricingRules.

messages.note: The network drops the response. The order exists, but the browser does not know.

messages.note: NETWORK_ERROR returns the screen to CART but keeps the same key.

messages.label: retry, same key
messages.note: The shopper presses Place order again. The reducer reuses the stored key.

messages.label: find order by key
messages.note: The key is already stored, so nothing is reserved or created again.

messages.label: 200 OR-1
messages.note: The replay returns the original order unchanged.

messages.label: ORDER_PLACED
messages.note: The screen moves to payment and counts down to payBy from the server.

walk.text: Screen state: step, quantities shown, quantities the server saved, key, error.
An edit shows at once, but only while the screen is in CART.
A save confirms the quantity; a failure rolls the shown value back.
Checkout starts once, only with items, and keeps the first key it saw.
Network, price and refusal errors return to CART with a message; the key stays.
A double click and two retries each bring a new key; the reducer keeps ck-1.

code.title: CartPage component
code.caption: A React component that renders state and dispatches events. Not run here.

walk.text: A ref blocks a second click that lands before React re-renders.
Dispatch the edit first, then save; the reply confirms or rolls back.
Use the stored key if a retry, else a new random one, and pass it in the event.
Map no response, a price change, any other error, and success to reducer events.
Distinct loading and empty states, never a blank page.
Errors render in an alert region; the button disables outside CART.

pitfalls: Disabling the button is not enough; the key and the reducer must also stop repeats.
Never generate a fresh key on retry; that turns a lost response into a second order.
Interview follow-up: a flash sale needs stock checks in the database, not the browser.

quiz.q: In the run, which key does the retry use?
quiz.why: CHECKOUT_CLICKED keeps `s.key` when one exists. NETWORK_ERROR left ck-1 in state, so the retry's ck-3 is ignored.

takeaway: One reducer owns the cart screen; one key per checkout makes retries safe.
